summary: Phase 149O.20D.1 -- HMIC v1.2 HBDC Content-Identity Binding Contract Repair: CONTRACT REPAIR ONLY, repairing finding B-149O.20D-1. Initial inspection confirmed repo clean, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.20D completed/complete/pushed, pcae health/check/status-coherence/push-check/runtime-inspect/notify-status all as expected, HMIC-001 v1.2 with HMIC-REQ-145 present, production still four-member contract_versions, HBDC-001 absent from the 24-file implementation_scope_digest set. Read docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md (all 51 sections, read before any edit), docs/contracts/HATP_CLASS_B_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md (all 30 sections, including SS17's own Rejected-alternatives analysis), the 149O.20A/20B/20C/20D phase documents, and production source (hatp_mandatory_certification.py) directly. Independently reproduced the defect before editing: confirmed, against the frozen pre-repair git snapshot (commit 5671448a) and live production, that (A) HBDC-001 was a contract_versions member, (B) its binding was version-header-comparison only, (C) HBDC-001 was absent from the 24-file implementation_scope_digest enumeration, and (D) a modeled same-version HBDC-001 byte mutation was invisible to both binding mechanisms -- a certification bound to pre-mutation bytes would continue validating against post-mutation bytes. Reconstructed the existing four dual-bound contracts' own content-binding mechanism directly from HMIC-REQ-050/053: their document bytes participate in implementation_scope_digest directly, a distinct binding from contract_versions' version-header check -- HBDC-001 had only the second binding. Evaluated four repair options (new contract_content_digest schema field; extending implementation_scope_digest; a separate bound-contract-only digest component; other repository-conventional mechanisms) and selected extending implementation_scope_digest (Option B): added HBDC-001's document as HMIC-REQ-050's twenty-fifth entry, giving it the identical dual binding the other four bound contracts already have, reusing the exact mechanism HMIC-REQ-145's own pre-repair text had already named as the available closing option, requiring no schema change. HMIC-001 remains v1.2 -- an in-place repair, not a version bump, mirroring the 149O.19.3R precedent for repairing a not-yet-independently-verified contract. HMIC-REQ-145 revised from a disclosed residual limitation to CLOSED, stating explicitly that the closure does not depend on repository actors honestly bumping a version string. HMIC-REQ-050/052/053/069 revised in place; no new requirement ID minted -- IDs remain HMIC-REQ-001-145 (145 total, mechanically verified gapless/no-duplicates). CIVC-1-12 unchanged in count; CIVC-5 strengthened in place to state the uniform five-member dual-binding consequence. Attack matrix grows from 36 to 37 rows: new row #37 (HBDC same-version content drift, now IMPLEMENTATION_MISMATCH, closing the gap); row #35 revised in place to point to it instead of restating the closed exception; row #36 unaffected. Independently confirmed the other four bound contracts' positions and content within HMIC-REQ-050 are byte-identical before and after this repair (diffed against the 5671448a snapshot) -- only the single new HBDC-001 entry differs. Independently confirmed HMIC-REQ-063's own text is byte-identical before and after (diffed against the same snapshot) -- this repair does not solve it. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20D_1_HMIC_V1_2_HBDC_CONTENT_IDENTITY_BINDING_REPAIR.md and tests/test_phase_149o_20d_1_hmic_v1_2_hbdc_content_identity_binding_repair.py (55 tests, all passed) that independently reproduces the pre-repair defect from the frozen 149O.20D git snapshot before verifying the repaired live contract. Updated 149O.20D's own test module, tests/test_phase_149o_20d_hmic_v1_2_hbdc_bound_contract_identity_evolution.py, in place per the 149O.19.3R repair precedent (43 tests, all passed; 1 skipped -- HMIC-001 itself), preserving the historical pre-repair 24-file constant as _PRE_REPAIR_24_FROZEN_PATHS rather than deleting it. Zero src/pcae/** and zero scripts/** files changed; HBDC-001 and all six other pre-existing bound contracts confirmed byte-unchanged in the working tree via git status --porcelain. No certifications.json/certification-bindings.json/active_certification.json exists anywhere in the repository. Broad HMIC/HBDC/149O.20-track sweep (pytest -k 'hmic or hbdc or 149o_20 or 149o_19_5', excluding one pre-existing fido2-import collection error present identically with and without this repair): repaired state 41 failed, 759 passed, 4 skipped; git-stash pre-phase baseline re-run: 23 failed, 723 passed, 4 skipped. Diffed precisely: the 18 additional failures are exclusively earlier phases' own live-text self-checks (149O.19.5B/5E.1-4/5F/5G, 149O.20A, 149O.20C) re-deriving implementation_scope_digest's file count or a fixed-commit git-diff/git-status self-check against the now-current contract text -- the identical repin-debt class 149O.20D's own amendment already caused for still-earlier phases, not a new class this repair's own logic introduces; spot-verified directly that 149O.20A's own git-status self-check reports exactly one offending line, the HMIC-001 contract this repair is chartered to modify. Fast Green (pytest -m fast_green, same exclusion): 68 failed, 6398 passed, 4 skipped; the 41-failure broad-sweep set above accounts for most of the delta, and the remaining 27 are entirely in production-source-dependent test files this phase's own zero-src/pcae-diff (independently confirmed empty via git status --porcelain -- src/pcae) proves cannot be caused by this repair, plus a handful more of the same fixed-commit-self-check class against unrelated pre-phase commits (149O.14, 149O.19.2, 149O.1G). This phase's own 55 new tests, and the 149O.20D module's updated 43 tests, all pass. Report trust and status-coherence/health/check all passing. Verdict: HMIC HBDC content-identity binding -- REPAIRED AT CONTRACT LEVEL -- same-version HBDC content drift now certification-visible -- PENDING INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION -- production alignment pending. B-149O.20D-1: REPAIRED AT CONTRACT LEVEL -- independent verification pending -- NOT CLOSED. HBDC-BINDING-GATE: CONTRACT CONTENT-BINDING REPAIR COMPLETE -- independent verification pending -- production alignment pending. Class-B: CONTRACT VERIFIED -- NOT PROVISIONED (unchanged). HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not claim HBDC binding complete or readiness for provisioning. Recommended next phase: 149O.20E -- HMIC v1.2 HBDC Bound-Contract Identity Independent Verification, scope now covering both the 149O.20D amendment and this repair.
